safe_mutations: palette swap for time of day

unsafe_mutations: disrupting the horizontal transition into the upper sky
removing the clustered shading on the peaks

pattern_regions.typical_size: thin, flat dashes of varying length

pattern_regions.orientation: vertical clusters along the bottom edges

important_colors.role: upper sky ambient and mountain shadows
lower sky glow and mist base

palette.palette_temperature: warm/cool split (cool upper sky and shadows, warm lower sky and mist)
palette.contrast_level: moderate to high (soft midtones with stark dark foreground)

lighting.direction: top left to bottom right (highlights on left side of clouds and mountain ridges)
lighting.warm_cool_balance: harmonious blend of cool purples and warm peaches
lighting.important_glows: broad atmospheric horizontal glow in the mist and lower sky layers

identified_effects: atmospheric perspective (distant layers are lighter and less detailed)
safe_changes: shifting hue for different times of day (e.g., golden hour or deep night)

pixel_characteristics.hard_pixel_edges: visible on the foreground pine trees and the sharp ridges of the primary mountains
pixel_characteristics.soft_edges: represented via smooth color banding in the sky and mist
pixel_characteristics.clustered_shading: heavy use in the central cumulus clouds to create a fluffy volumetric look, and on the mountain faces to show rock texture
pixel_characteristics.gradients: achieved through distinct horizontal color steps (banding) in the sky and mist layers
pixel_characteristics.dithering: minimal traditional dithering; relies more on dense color ramps and clustered pixels
pixel_characteristics.texture: puffy/bubbly clouds, jagged/sharp mountains, smooth banded sky
pixel_characteristics.native_pixel_scale_feel: medium-high resolution pixel art, clean and modern

region_relationships: primary_mountain_range occludes the lower sky and some stratus clouds
central_cumulus_clouds overlap the upper sky and stratus clouds
valley_mist overlaps the base of the primary_mountain_range and foreground_rolling_hills
foreground_trees_left and foreground_trees_right occlude all other layers behind them

must_remain_stable: horizontal layering of depth (sky -> mountains -> mist -> foreground)
the central prominence of the highest mountain peak and the cloud formation above it
dark framing silhouettes at the bottom corners
safe_to_change: overall color palette (maintaining atmospheric depth logic)
placement of thin horizontal stratus clouds
